title: Units move only into the activated system, from adjacent systems
text: Units move only during an activation and only into the activated system, from any number of systems adjacent to it. Units cannot move into a system that was not activated.

title: Units cannot leave a system that contains their own leader
text: Units cannot move out of a system containing a leader of their own faction, even one without tactic values. Leaders placed earlier in the phase stay until Refresh and keep locking their systems.

exceptions.text: A leader on the "Rebel Base" space only locks units on that space, not units in the base's system.
A captured Rebel leader does not stop Rebel units from leaving its system.

keywords: leave a system with my leader

title: Enemy units or leaders do not pin units
text: Units may leave a system that contains enemy units or enemy leaders; only a leader of their own faction keeps them in place.
rationale: The movement rules list the restrictions exhaustively (adjacency, impassable areas, transport, immobile units, own leader) and none mentions enemy units or leaders; retreat has its own separate rules. Silence of the source, not an explicit statement.

title: Adjacency and impassable areas
text: Two systems that share a border are adjacent. Units may cross the orange region borders but cannot pass through the impassable areas shaded in light red.

title: Immobile units never move
text: A unit with the immobile icon cannot move: the Rebel structures (Shield Generator, Ion Cannon) and the Death Star Under Construction.

title: Abilities that move units follow the movement rules
text: When a card lets a player move units, all movement rules still apply (transport capacity, immobile units and so on). Only an ability that says to ignore transport restrictions lets restricted units move without a carrier leaving their system.

title: Moving into enemy units causes combat
text: If, after units move into the activated system, the other faction has units there, combat follows (only in a theater where both sides have units).

title: Mission movement is also blocked by own leaders
text: A mission that moves units (for example Rapid Mobilization) cannot move Rebel units out of a system that contains a friendly leader.

title: A leader on the Rebel Base space blocks mission movement from it
text: With a Rebel leader on the "Rebel Base" space, a mission such as Lead the Strike Team cannot move units from the base; only cards that explicitly override this (such as Plan the Assault) can.

title: Transport capacity
text: Ground units and TIE Fighters move only by transport: each moving ship carries from its own system up to its transport capacity (faction sheet), one place per unit. X-wings and Y-wings need no transport.

title: Transport restriction icon
text: Units with the transport restriction icon (ground units, TIE Fighters) move only together with transport-capacity units leaving the same system; ships staying behind or already at the destination cannot carry them.

title: Transport capacities used by the engine
text: Capacities used by core-v1: Star Destroyer 6, Assault Carrier 4, Super Star Destroyer 8, Death Star 8; Corellian Corvette 2, Rebel Transport 4, Mon Calamari Cruiser 4; X-wing, Y-wing and TIE Fighter 0. Rebel values and the other Rebel faction sheet stats still have to be checked against the physical sheet.
rationale: The rules say capacity is printed on the faction sheet but give no numbers in text. The Imperial values were read from the faction sheet illustration (LTP p.4) in SWR-005; the Rebel values come from a fan data set only, because the Rebel sheet values are not readable in the text layer.
